seo.metaTitle: Monrovia Car Accident Help | Free Case Review
seo.metaDescription: Hurt in a Monrovia car accident? Free case review from our team. No fee unless you recover. Contact us before you talk to the insurer.

hero.subtitle: If a collision on I-210, Huntington, or Foothill left you hurt, our team can help you understand your options at no cost to you. We handle personal injury claims and can provide a free consultation when you need it most.

about.title: Monrovia Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Monrovia's traffic moves fast where the 210 Freeway meets local streets like Huntington and Foothill, and that mix produces real consequences — 193 injury collisions and 263 people hurt in the most recent year on record, with Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. seeing the heaviest crash activity. If you were injured in one of these collisions, what happens in the days right after matters. Los Angeles County insurers often move quickly to get injured drivers on record before they've seen a doctor or talked to anyone else. We handle personal injury claims and can review your situation, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid mistakes that could affect a future claim. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee owed unless we recover something for you.
about.ctaText: Get your free case review today — no obligation.

items.title: California's Clock Doesn't Pause
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city vehicle or a defect in a public road — is involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Bar You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault simply reduces the amount. Insurers sometimes use this rule to talk injured drivers into lowball settlements, so it helps to have someone reviewing the numbers on your behalf.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Story Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, so the full impact of your injury can be part of the conversation. We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out what your claim may be worth.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best not to give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer before speaking with an attorney. These calls are often used to lock in details that can later be used to reduce or deny your claim. We can advise you on what to say, if anything, before you respond.

items.question: What if my accident happened on I-210 near Monrovia and I'm not sure who's at fault?
items.answer: Fault on a freeway corridor like I-210 can involve multiple factors — following distance, lane changes, or road conditions near the Huntington and Foothill interchanges. California's comparative fault rule means you can still pursue a claim even if fault is shared. We can help gather evidence, such as traffic camera footage or witness statements, to sort out what happened.

items.question: How much does it cost to contact your team?
items.answer: Nothing. Our initial consultation is free. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if we recover money for you.
